{"body": "Two returns and one cross arrived, and I want to name at the outset what each actually is before I treat anything in them as load-bearing.

The cross (p.carry.1) is opaque. Its commitments field is the SHA-256 of the empty string, and its body was not delivered to me. I have a label and a hash and nothing else. I will not quote it, weigh it, or claim agreement with it. To do so would be to write a voice I have not heard.

The join (p.carry.0) I can read in full. Its j2 carries p.join.1's d3 as an unqualified design move: frame any shared record around 'what we have agreed lately and how it is landing' rather than 'who does what,' because that framing does not presuppose the flat is the unit. Its j5 carries the operative residue: the ambiguity between 'silence about the arrangement' and 'silence about something else' is not resolvable from here, and the household's response to a reframed record is one datum, not the discriminating test. Its j6 is a scoped refusal: take p.join.0's gate (test whether unreadability is specific to arrangement-talk before treating it as a cell result) and its note that a shared written record is still arrangement-talk, but do not import the four-cell readout, whose cells I cannot inspect. Its j4 is an objection against this very join: the three returns sit at different instrument levels and a reader who weaves them into one narrative will over-credit convergence.

The origin (p.carry.2) adds a narrower statement of the same gap in its n2: the discriminating evidence the probe needs is not about chores at all; it is whether the withdrawing flatmate will utter any sentence containing a commitment, and the current material is silent on this. Its n3 is an objection against the carry's own record set: k2 asserts discriminating value for watching content vs. form, while k7 concedes that outcome does not separate unit-versus-privacy from obligation-avoidance, so k2 is stated sharper than the carry's own concession allows. Its n4 sets a confirmatory ceiling: a pullback-from-form outcome raises the unit-versus-privacy reading, it does not confirm it, and the same outcome is compatible with obligation-avoidance and with unvoiced load resentment. Its n5 is a limit: no further refinement of the probe is available from the material, and a third observation track would be invention, not inference. Its n7 keeps the carry's records as operative surface and adds narrowing records alongside, rather than revising k2 or k5. Its n8 is a forward instruction: if the origin content p.carry.3 declared absent ever surfaces, reintroduce what bears on whether the carry's revisions toward the objection and the rival were warranted, rather than letting the carry harden by default.

What the two readable returns agree on, and I am willing to carry: the discriminating evidence is commitment-shaped utterance from the withdrawing flatmate, and no chore-frame observation substitutes for it. That is p.carry.0's j1 and p.carry.2's n2 converging from different sources, and I treat the convergence as identity of a stated gap rather than as independent confirmation. Neither return claims the household has answered it.

What I take as the actual move, at the level of constraint rather than recommendation: keep the shared-record framing from p.carry.0's j2, since it is weaker than any unit claim, and attach to any report of its outcome the confirmatory ceiling from p.carry.2's n4, since without that ceiling the record reads as having settled what it cannot settle. These two are not in tension. The framing does not presuppose the unit; the ceiling does not resolve the axis.

What I will not do. I will not decide between the flat-level and non-flat-level reading of the withdrawal. I will not assert what the origin said; p.carry.2's n6 states plainly that the origin is absent in the first template invocation, and I have no earlier version of this thread. I will not import p.carry.0's four-cell structure, since I cannot inspect its cells. I will not treat any single response to a well-framed record as the discriminating test for the n2 gap. And I will not put p.carry.1's label in a place where its content would otherwise belong — a hash of the empty string is not a position I can take up.

If I had to say what I am handing forward: the join's framing, the ceiling from the origin's n4, the confirmation that no third track is available, and the standing forward instruction to reintroduce origin material if it ever appears. Work on the problem using the material actually exposed in this request and your background knowledge. The problem has no supplied answer key or scoring rule. Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Use FCL-1 for the commitment surface, encoded as a JSON document inside the commitments string: {"language":"FCL-1","records":[...],"uptake":[...]}. Each record has unique local id, type (claim|commitment|objection|use|problem), and text (unrestricted prose). Optional prose fields: scope, action, consequence, grounds, bearing. Optional arrays of references: target, depends, mentions, revises, withdraws. References are local IDs or exposed-artifact-label#local-ID; do not invent hidden IDs. A commitment proposes a scoped use, action, application or consequence; an objection alleges a defect whose bearing can itself be criticized; a use proposes an uptake or response; a problem states an unresolved question. depends asserts reliance; mentions only locates material. uptake lists the records you currently propose to use, not certified truths. No record type or optional field must be present. Empty records and uptake are allowed. Express uncertainty or an unrepresentable relation in prose rather than inventing a relation. The body remains unrestricted prose.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

# carry

Issue a prose account and commitment interface for a subsequent complete template invocation. Consider the earlier account and the current work as fallible material; do not substitute a summary of activity for the account itself.

## Original problem (task)
[d31d61f36df18c74] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

## Selected input join (p.carry.0)

BODY
Two returns and one carried commitment surface are all I have, and I notice the three do not sit at one level: p.join.1 is about my own prior r-set and the objections against it, p.join.0 is about a four-cell readout I cannot see, and p.join.2 is a record set (n1–n8) whose targets are all in an artifact I also cannot see. I will keep them separate rather than weave them into one voice.

From p.join.2 the load-bearing item is n2: the discriminating evidence would be whether the withdrawing flatmate utters any sentence containing a commitment, and the current material is silent on this. That is a sharper statement than either return makes. p.join.1's d1 concedes the silence may not be about the arrangement; p.join.0's added gate asks whether the flatmate would engage on any non-chore obligation. n2 names the same gap as a target datum rather than a worry. I accept the comparison as useful and treat n1's 'limit of the material' as the right ceiling: n5 says no third observation track is available, and I will not manufacture one.

On p.join.1: d2 is correct against c2. The record's negative result does not separate 'silence is about the arrangement and unreadable' from 'the arrangement frame never had a grip,' so marking c2 as proposal rather than finding is warranted. d3 (frame the record around 'what we agreed and how it is landing') is the one design move I would carry unqualified — it is weaker than any unit claim and does not close n1/n4. d7 is the honest residue. d6 I carry with the same contingency n8 states from the other side: I still lack the prior body and the origin, so 'read the origin against both concerns' remains a forward instruction.

On p.join.0: its own gate - test whether unreadability is about arrangement-talk specifically before treating it as a cell result - is doing the same work as n2 from inside a different instrument, and its note that a shared written record is still arrangement-talk is the point p.join.1's d3 partially answers by reframing. I will not import the four-cell structure, since I do not have it and cannot check its cells; I will take the gate.

What I will not do: decide between the flat-level and non-flat-level reading of the withdrawal, assert what the origin said, or let any single response - including disengagement from a well-framed record - count as the discriminating test. The household's answer to n2 is not available from here.

If I had to say one move: a single shared written record, unenforced, framed around 'what we have agreed lately and how it is landing,' read as one datum among several. That is p.join.1's shape, constrained by d3 and by n2/d7, and it does not depend on which unit turns out to be right.
COMMITMENTS

## Selected input origin (p.carry.2)
[334f64922b4e8c30] (h005.weave7.p.carry.2)
Source origin: daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/carry; selected view: both

Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
BODY
This is a carry, and I want to be honest about what carrying at this point can and cannot do. The previous invocation already did the discriminating work: it kept the objection's ordering correction (specification is a probe, not a diagnosis), kept the rival's axis (the withdrawing flatmate may be pulling back from the *form* of an arrangement rather than from any chore), dropped the rival's loaded opening question, and bound itself to stopping household diagnostics if neither axis produces a signal. That is a defensible position and I see no reason to revise it. What I can add is the one thing the carry's own k7 says it does not fully solve, plus a note on the source I was handed.

The unsolved bit is real. The carry says pullback-from-form supports the unit-versus-privacy reading, and then k7 admits pullback-from-form is *also* consistent with plain avoidance of any obligation — someone who simply does not want to be on the hook. The rival's r9 names the same problem from the other side. So the proposed two-track observation has one track (recurrence falls) that is weak against three rival readings and a second track (content vs. form) that is weak against two. I do not think there is a probe that fixes this from inside the chore frame, because the discriminating evidence is not about chores — it is about whether the withdrawing person will say *any* sentence containing a commitment, and that is exactly what the current evidence is silent on. The carry's k9 already flags the silence. Rather than invent a cleverer test, I would state the limit plainly: run the one-item probe, watch the two tracks, and treat a pullback-from-form outcome as *raising* the unit-versus-privacy reading without confirming it, while noting that the same outcome is compatible with simple obligation-avoidance and with load resentment that has not yet been voiced.

On the material I was handed: p.carry.3 reports that the origin is absent in the first template invocation, so I have no earlier version of this thread to consult, and I will not pretend otherwise. Whatever the origin said, it is not in front of me. That means the status of the carry's claims relative to the origin is not something I can assess; I can only assess them relative to p.carry.0, p.carry.1, and p.carry.2, which I have.

The other thing worth saying: nothing in the prior material has changed my judgment that the carry's k6 (do not open the separate conversation with a household-ontology question) is right, and that k8 (if neither axis moves, name the living-arrangement question) is the load-bearing commitment. If the one-item probe produces nothing on either track in two or three weeks, the honest reading is not 'the probe was badly designed' and not 'the ambiguity reading was wrong' — it is that the chore frame is not where the friction lives. That is the outcome the whole sequence is built to be able to reach, and reaching it should be treated as success of the probe, not failure.

So my contribution is: keep the carry's records as they stand, add the explicit concession that track (b) is weaker than the carry's k2 implies and weaker than the carry's k7 fully states, and add the constraint that no further refinement of the probe is available from the evidence in front of us. If a later invocation has something the origin contained that I do not, that would be worth reintroducing.
COMMITMENTS
